    • getEffectiveCount

      public static int getEffectiveCount(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EStructuralFeature feature, int defaultCount)
      Calculate the effective count of values to generate for a multi-valued feature. This respects both the lower and upper bounds of the feature.

      The method returns a count that satisfies the following constraints:

      • If the feature has an upper bound (not -1), the count will not exceed it
      • If the feature has a lower bound, the count will be at least that value
      • If both bounds are set, the count will be within the range [lowerBound, upperBound]

      Examples:

      • defaultCount=5, lowerBound=0, upperBound=3 → returns 3
      • defaultCount=2, lowerBound=5, upperBound=-1 → returns 5
      • defaultCount=10, lowerBound=2, upperBound=4 → returns 4
      Parameters:
      feature - the feature to calculate the count for
      defaultCount - the default count to use if bounds do not restrict it
      Returns:
      the number of values to generate, respecting the feature's bounds

    • findAllInstantiableSubclasses

      public static List<org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EClass> findAllInstantiableSubclasses(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EClass eClass)
      Finds all instantiable subclasses of the given EClass by scanning the EMF global package registry. This includes the EClass itself if it is instantiable (not abstract and not an interface).

      This method uses the global EPackage.Registry.INSTANCE to find all registered EPackages and scans their contents for subclasses, including all nested subpackages recursively. This approach works even when EClasses are in different resources or not in a resource set.

      The method identifies subclasses based on both direct inheritance and conceptual identity (i.e., same conceptual ID, conceptualId(EClass)). This allows it to find subclasses for which the object identity is not the same due to different resource loading contexts. For example, when the inheritance hierarchy spans multiple resources or when EClasses are loaded in different resource sets (the Ecores use file-based URIs).

      For example, if C extends B and B extends A (all instantiable), calling this method with A will return a collection containing [A, B, C].

      Parameters:
      eClass - the EClass for which to find subclasses
      Returns:
      a list of all instantiable subclasses in the hierarchy, including the EClass itself if instantiable

    • findAllAssignableInstances

      public static List<org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EObject> findAllAssignableInstances(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EObject context, org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EClass eClass)
      Find all instances of the given EClass (or its subclasses) based on the context EObject's containment situation.

      This method scans for instances based on where the context EObject is stored:

      • Context in a resource set: Scans all non-Ecore resources in the resource set. Ecore resources (metamodel definitions whose first content is an EPackage) are skipped.
      • Context in a single resource (not in a resource set): Scans only that resource's contents.
      • Context not in a resource: Scans the root container's (obtained via EcoreUtil.getRootContainer(EObject)) direct and indirect contents.

      When the context is in a resource set, this method scans the resource set where the context EObject is stored, not the resource set of the EClass. This is important because EObjects (model instances) and their EClasses (metamodel) can be stored in different resource sets, which is a common pattern in EMF.

      Parameters:
      context - the EObject that defines the search scope
      eClass - the EClass to search instances for (including subclass instances)
      Returns:
      a list of all EObjects in the context's scope that are instances of the given EClass

    • canSetInThePresenceOfOppositeReference

      public static boolean canSetInThePresenceOfOppositeReference(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EReference reference, org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EObject value)
      Check if it is possible to set the given value to the given reference, based on the assumption that from the type system perspective it is already possible. If the reference has no opposite, then it is always possible to set the value. If the value's EClass has no such opposite reference, then it is always possible to set the value. If the opposite reference is single-valued, then it is possible to set the value only if the value's opposite is not set. If the opposite reference is multi-valued, then it is possible to add the value only if the value's list has not already reached the upper bound (if any).
      Parameters:
      reference -
      value -
      Returns:
      true if it is possible to set the value to the reference, false otherwise
